## Key terms

{{< glossary media-channel art-style sound-effect ambience feedback diegetic accessibility player-experience >}}

## 2.1 The media inventory

An analysis starts with a description: an **inventory** of every media element,
sorted by **media channel** — **visual** (art style, characters, animation,
effects), **audio** (music, sound effects, voices, ambience), **text and
narrative**, **cinematic** (cut-scenes, trailers) and **interface** (menus,
HUD).

![Ember Trail: one screen, six media elements.](images/annotated-screen.png){width=94%}

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 1 · Which channel?"}
Choose the media channel of each element.

::: {.match}
The rounded shapes and warm palette shared by all the characters.
:   visual

The wind that blows in the background.
:   audio

A quest log that describes the next task.
:   text and narrative

A one-minute animated scene between two chapters.
:   cinematic

The pause button and the coin counter.
:   interface
:::
:::

## 2.2 The functions of media

Each element has a job: **feedback** (what happened?), **guidance** (where
next?), **mood** (how should it feel?), **narrative** (what is the story?) and
**identity** (which game is this?). One element often has several functions.
Analysis names the element, its function *and* its effect on the player.

::: {.callout-note title="Watch out!"}
"There is music in the menu" only describes. "The slow flute theme in the
menu sets a calm mood before play begins" analyses.
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 2 · Which function?"}
Choose the main function of each element.

::: {.match}
A chime and a flash when a coin is collected.
:   feedback

A glowing door at the end of a dark corridor.
:   guidance

Slow strings in a farewell scene.
:   mood

A ruined statue that hints at an old war.
:   narrative

The theme tune that players recognise at once.
:   identity
:::
:::

## 2.3 Inside or outside the game world

**Diegetic** elements belong to the game world — its characters could perceive
them (the crackle of a fire, footsteps). **Non-diegetic** elements exist only
for the player (background music, the HUD). For interfaces there are four
kinds: diegetic, non-diegetic, **spatial** (in the space, not in the story: a
floating name tag) and **meta** (in the story, not in the space: blood on the
screen). Diegetic design adds immersion; non-diegetic design adds clarity.

![Four kinds of interface elements.](images/diegesis.png){width=70%}

{{< sim file="sims/sound-stage.html" poster="sims/sound-stage.png" title="Sound Stage: inside or outside the world?" kind="game" height="600" >}}

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 3 · Diegetic or not?"}
Choose the kind of each element. You can use an answer more than once.

::: {.match}
The crackle of a campfire that grows louder as you come closer.
:   diegetic

The flute music that plays during the whole level.
:   non-diegetic

A health bar in the corner of the screen.
:   non-diegetic

A name floating above a character's head.
:   spatial

Blood spatter on the screen when the hero is hurt.
:   meta

An ammunition counter printed on the side of the gun.
:   diegetic
:::
:::

## 2.4 Evaluating media

Evaluate against criteria, not taste: **coherence** (one style and tone),
**clarity** (important information is quick to read), **fit** (genre,
audience, moment), **technical quality** (resolution, compression, loudness)
and **accessibility** (never rely on one channel; offer subtitles). Write each
point as **claim → evidence → effect** on the player.

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 4 · Which criterion?"}
Choose the criterion that each problem violates, or the right term.

::: {.match}
A photo-realistic tree in a cartoon world.
:   coherence

A red warning on a red background.
:   clarity

Cheerful music during a sad scene.
:   fit

Distorted, clipping audio.
:   technical quality

No subtitles, and colour is the only danger signal.
:   accessibility

The three parts of an analytical statement.
:   claim, evidence, effect
:::
:::

## Game challenge: analysing Ember Trail {.challenge}

Work alone. Use every section of today.

**Ember Trail** is a 2D adventure game for phones: a young fox crosses a
forest at night to return home. The art style is soft and rounded, the
palette warm against deep blue, the music a solo flute with wind ambience.
The thin orange health bar sits on a sunset sky of almost the same colour.
The coin "ting" is louder than the characters' voices.

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 5 · Your analysis (harder)"}
Choose the right term.

::: {.match extra="coherence|mood"}
The fox's footsteps get louder as it walks on the wooden bridge.
:   diegetic

The criterion that the health bar fails.
:   clarity

The function of a heartbeat sound added when health is low.
:   feedback

The criterion that the loud coin sound fails.
:   technical quality

Players recognise the game by its flute theme. The function.
:   identity
:::
:::

## Summary {.summary}

- Four steps: inventory → functions → diegetic or not → evaluation.
- Five channels: visual, audio, text and narrative, cinematic, interface.
- Five functions: feedback, guidance, mood, narrative, identity.
- Diegetic = inside the world; non-diegetic = only for the player; plus spatial and meta interfaces.
- Criteria: coherence, clarity, fit, technical quality, accessibility.
- Write claim → evidence → effect.
